subject: Request: hard geo-segregation and model constraint for PHI workflows
messages:
From: Annie Park <annie@stellarishealth.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Contracts Team <contracts@stellarishealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Request: hard geo-segregation and model constraint for PHI workflows

Hi Sofia / Grace,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We reviewed the security questionnaire with the clinical ops and legal teams and there are two show-stoppers for us to move forward:

- All inference for PHI-bearing payloads must be processed within the EU (no routing to other regions under any circumstance).
- For these PHI flows we require a locked model selection — the request must not fallback to any other model variant or lower-capacity tier (i.e., forced use of our approved model variant v1.9-q4).

Both requirements are non-negotiable due to regulatory constraints. I attached our security requirements and a simple data-flow diagram that highlights the PHI path.

Can Redwood confirm feasibility and provide a short mutual action plan (MAP) and timelines? We are aiming to close procurement by the end of July.

Attachments: stellaris_requirements_v2.pdf, data_flow_diagram.png

Best,
Annie Park
Head of Integrations, Stellaris Health
annie@stellarishealth.com
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Annie Park <annie@stellarishealth.com>, Contracts Team <contracts@stellarishealth.com>
Date: Mon, 28 Jun 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: hard geo-segregation and model constraint for PHI workflows

Annie — thanks for the clear ask and the attachments. Looping in Marcus (engineering) and Lauren (product legal intake) so we can evaluate constraints and propose an implementation plan.

High-level questions we need to surface up-front:
1) Is Stellaris expecting a hosted Redwood deployment (hosted API) with contractual region guarantees, or will they require Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem) in an EU data center?
2) For the locked model variant (v1.9-q4) — do you expect Redwood to maintain that binary indefinitely for you, or would you accept a pinned lineage with a migration clause?
3) Any SLO tradeoffs on latency/availability you are willing to accept if we enforce a strict no-fallback policy?

Marcus / Lauren — can you confirm technical feasibility for a hard EU-only routing policy that absolutely prevents cross-region fallback and also enforces a model pin without automatic fallback? If we can do this on hosted, we should also call out required capacity (dedicated pool) and any SLA adjustments.

I'll consolidate answers into a MAP and proposed dates for review with their procurement/legal.

Thanks,
Sofia Ivanova
Senior Account Lead, Redwood Inference
sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>, Annie Park <annie@stellarishealth.com>
Date: Tue, 29 Jun 2027 08:46:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Request: hard geo-segregation and model constraint for PHI workflows

Sofia / team — technical assessment below. Short answer: feasible, but requires dedicated capacity and explicit contract-level exceptions.

Details / constraints:
- Geo-segregation (hard EU-only): We can enforce region-locking at the routing layer by tagging requests and configuring per-tenant routing policies that exclude non-EU pools. However, this eliminates our usual cross-region fallbacks that protect against zone outages. That increases outage blast radius for the tenant.

- No-fallback / forced model selection: We can implement a per-route policy that only allows exactly the pinned model artifact (e.g., model v1.9-q4) and returns an error when the artifact is unavailable. This is a straight-forward config in the control plane, but the artifact must be hosted in a dedicated pool or pinned storage to avoid eviction/GC on our autoscaling nodes.

- Capacity & performance: To keep latency acceptable and maintain availability without fallback, we need a reserved GPU pool in the EU region (dedicated capacity). Estimated starting commit: 2xA10 or 1xA100 equivalency depending on expected QPS and max sequence lengths — I need the expected traffic profile to firm this up.

- Operational changes: No prefix caching/burst-sharing across tenants for this policy. Monitoring and runbooks need to be adjusted — we recommend a separate on-call rotation or escalation path for tenants using hard locks.

- Optics on SLA: Because we will not route to cross-region backups, any regional outage will impact availability. Product/legal should consider an SLA carve-out or an availability target that reflects the lack of fallback.

Action items for us before we send a MAP to the customer:
1) Product: confirm whether we support pin retention guarantees (Lauren).
2) SRE: draft recommended reserved capacity sizes given traffic estimate (I'll need QPS, p95 latency targets, and seq length distribution).
3) Sales/CS: confirm whether the customer is OK with an SLA carve-out and an estimated uplift in cost.

Happy to jump on a call with Stellaris to walk through trade-offs.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin, Staff Engineer — Serving Runtime
marcus_lin@redwood.ai

2) Engineering (Marcus) will produce a capacity estimate and recommended instance sizing request by Tue (2027-07-06) — Marcus, please include cost uplift ballpark.
3) I will schedule a 30-minute MAP review for Thurs 2027-07-08 at 10:00 CEST (please confirm availability).
4) Contracts (Stellaris) — if you can share the procurement timeline and any specific procurement contacts, we'll throw together an amendment draft and a short SOW.
